verdicts.correction: The only construct that forces the 2023 directory is ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL on F-BACK. Line sequential organization is new in 2023 (the ISO 2023 new-features list at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:1105 has 'Line Sequential file organization'). Everything that sentence 2 needs (>>TURN, USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION, RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT, EC-REPORT-ACTIVE/INACTIVE, FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS) exists from 2002, and the writer's own note says so. The readback is also not spec-derived. F-B is a report file with the default (record) sequential organization, and whether its physical bytes read back through a LINE SEQUENTIAL connector as one 'B-DETAIL' line (after skipping blank lines) depends on the implementor's representation of the report file and its line advancing, not on the standard. The 'blank lines skipped' filter points to observed output. The absence of an INACTIVE line after GENERATE DET-B already proves that R-B was initiated. Fix: remove F-BACK, BACK-REC, WS-EOF and the readback loop, so the .out ends at 'AFTER-2 H=3'. Then move the case to tests/conformance/2002/, the lowest edition where every construct exists. Its expected output is these five lines: HANDLED=EC-REPORT-ACTIVE / AFTER-1 H=1 / HANDLED=EC-REPORT-ACTIVE / HANDLED=EC-REPORT-ACTIVE / AFTER-2 H=3. I re-derived those five lines from §14.9.21.4 GR2 (the report is active, so EC-REPORT-ACTIVE with no other effect) and GR5, then §14.9.33.4 GR2a. The row's 85 cell (sentence 1 only) still has no 85 golden; a plain two-name INITIATE whose second report is shown active by a GENERATE would cover it.

all_upheld_flag: Not all upheld: GR-14.9.21.4-5 is overturned. What I tried on each golden. LOCK-53: I re-derived all four lines. The records are distinct per connector, so no 51. C18 holds 0 locks, so no 54. The 256 records exist because SEEDF writes 1..256. §12.4.5.9.4 GR7 sets the maximums at >=255 per run unit and >=15 per connector, and CONFORMANCE DOC-A.1-154/155 documents 255/15. EC-I-O-RECORD-OPERATION is NF (Table), so a 53 does not terminate the run unit. §9.1.16 has CLOSE release the locks, and the commit/rollback exception does not apply. A higher run-unit ceiling would print 00 instead of 53, so the golden discriminates. All of it is 2002 syntax. IF-DIRECTIVE MULTILINE: I traced all 7 lines. That included the nested IF/EVALUATE in the included text-1, the DEFINE/OVERRIDE in the omitted text having no effect, and IS NOT DEFINED. >>EVALUATE and >>DEFINE are in the 2002 directive band (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE 7.21). An implementation that included only the first line of a text would differ. NEGATIVES: for each, I checked that the program is otherwise legal. For the PERFORM Format 3 WHEN exception-name-1 form I rendered the diagram text. I checked that the .err names the violation: 1619 prints the truncated operand, and 1605 is this rule's own message. The mid-line case pins the generic COBOL0307 "unexpected '>'". I let it stand because §7.3.16.3 SR1 and §7.3.3 SR2 require rejection, the only defect is the '>>' placement, and an implementation lax on SR1 would accept the program. It is still the weakest of the four. CITATIONS: I ran cite.py --check on all 17 quoted citations and every one returned OK with the matching clause/item. RESUME golden: the order of output lines is right (EC-REPORT-ACTIVE is Fatal, but RESUME from its declarative is legal). What fails is the edition placement and the implementation-observed LINE SEQUENTIAL readback.
